clue.text: Nurse gets right in the fashion

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A nurse keeps up with the latest styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is the current direction of taste, a synonym for fashion.

clue.text: A pair of leaders is proverbially better than one

definitions.text: A pair of leaders is proverbially better than one

parts.words: A pair of leaders is proverbially better than one
parts.note: leaders read literally as heads, and a pair of them as the proverb that says a second mind helps solve a problem

explanation.surface: A remark on a proverb about having two people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'two heads are better than one'; 'leaders' stands for heads.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says two minds working together beat a single one, and leaders are heads.

clue.text: At the end of the day it's the object of egalitarians

definitions.text: At the end of the day
definitions.meaning: the close of the day, the time after sunset
egalitarians aim at making everyone equal, levelling things out

explanation.surface: A remark that, ultimately, equality is what reformers want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' poses as the cliche meaning 'ultimately', but it literally names the time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the later part of the day, and making things level is what egalitarians pursue.

clue.text: Make a run for it!

parts.note: an order to sprint off quickly, which is also a mild exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: A shouted order to flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprint off suddenly is to rush, and the exclamation 'Make a run for it!' urges a quick dart.

clue.text: Could be a Manxman admitting to character assassination

definitions.meaning: a man from the Isle of Man lives on an island in the Irish Sea
read as a confession, '...', owning up to defaming someone

explanation.surface: A man from the Isle of Man owns up to smearing someone's reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is split I + SLANDER: someone admitting to slander says 'I slander'. A Manxman comes from the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Isle of Man is an island dweller, and slander is the assassination of a person's character.

clue.text: Come, dear, a ring's in order for this wedding too

indicators.note: putting the letters in order means rearranging them into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, with its S

explanation.surface: A proposal: come, darling, a ring is ready for another wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' sounds like 'appropriate', but it tells you to rearrange COME DEAR A RINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A further wedding after a first one is a remarriage, the 'too' marking it as another.

clue.text: Everyone has a yen to make a firm friend

parts.note: everyone means all
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, the yen

explanation.surface: Everybody with a craving makes a close companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a longing but is the currency, giving Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone firmly on your side, a loyal partner.

clue.text: Old peer is moved to express intense disapproval

indicators.note: the letters are moved around, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly lord is stirred to voice strong condemnation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is moved' sounds like being emotionally touched, but it means the letters of OLD PEER are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something is to condemn it strongly.

clue.text: Gives cheering support to radicals

definitions.meaning: cheers a team on, as a fan does
radicals are the base parts of words or plants, their origins

explanation.surface: A remark that someone backs political extremists.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer a team is to back it, and radical comes from the Latin for the base of a plant.

clue.text: The high regard which the fit patient doubtless feels for his doctor

definitions.text: The high regard which the fit patient doubtless feels for his doctor

parts.words: The high regard which the fit patient doubtless feels for his doctor
parts.note: a phrase meaning proper esteem, read literally as the esteem of a well person for the one who keeps them well

explanation.surface: A thought on how a well patient regards their physician.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a proper, wary esteem, and a patient in good health would feel it for the physician who keeps them so.

clue.text: Manage to discover what a bishop's position is

definitions.meaning: to run or supervise

definitions.text: to discover what a bishop's position is
definitions.meaning: a bishop sits above a diocese, his see, so his position is over the see

explanation.surface: A question about how to find out a bishop's rank.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's diocese is his see, so his position is 'over see'.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to run things, and a bishop is placed above his diocese.

clue.text: The song was one Odysseus at first found charming

definitions.meaning: a type of Caribbean song with topical lyrics

definitions.text: one Odysseus at first found charming
definitions.meaning: the nymph who kept Odysseus on her island for seven years in Homer's Odyssey

explanation.surface: A tune that the Greek hero first liked.
explanation.walkthrough: A calypso is a Caribbean song form; in the Odyssey the nymph Calypso holds Odysseus captive on her island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinidadian song form shares its name with the Homeric nymph who held the hero.

clue.text: In this verse pictures of the heroes can be found

definitions.text: In this verse pictures of the heroes can be found

indicators.note: the letters sit in the run of the two clue words that follow, across the word break

explanation.surface: A remark that heroic portraits appear in this poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of 'verse pictures'; the whole clue also describes a heroic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrative poem about heroes and their deeds is the heroic kind of verse.

clue.text: Highland dance which might well appeal to the indulgent pleasure-seeker

definitions.meaning: a lively Scottish solo dance

definitions.text: might well appeal to the indulgent pleasure-seeker
definitions.meaning: a short spell of wild self-indulgence or a brief affair

explanation.surface: A Scottish dance that suits a hedonist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland Fling is a traditional Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland dance has the same name as a brief spree of pleasure.

clue.text: The intelligence which may mean the end of you and me

parts.note: no more of something, its end
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A sinister threat that information may finish two people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The intelligence' looks like spy information but means common sense; 'the end of you and me' gives NO US, no more of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is practical good sense, the Greek word for mind.

clue.text: It may indicate a cold scorn

definitions.meaning: a noisy intake through the nose, a sign of a cold
to show contempt, as in turning one's nose up

explanation.surface: A remark on a chilly sign of disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: A runny nose makes one draw breath noisily, and the same noise expresses disdain.

clue.text: In the United States English is employed

parts.note: taken as written
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: In America the English language is spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' looks like having a job but means being used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being used at the moment is in employment.

clue.text: O, Ann, might greed abnormally selfish produce such an attitude?

definitions.text: O, Ann, might greed abnormally selfish produce such an attitude?

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an abnormal way, so they are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks Ann whether selfishness could cause a mean attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abnormally' rearranges O ANN MIGHT GREED; the phrase comes from Aesop's fable of a dog lying in the hay so the ox cannot eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The fable's dog keeps others from what it cannot use itself, a spiteful selfishness.

clue.text: Have confidence about American currency of late

indicators.note: one piece goes about, around, the other

parts.note: to have confidence in is to rely on
a cent is a US coin

explanation.surface: Trust the dollar's recent value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like the state of being current, which suits 'of late', but here it is money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately and of late both mean in the recent past.

clue.text: Aesthetic creed of the dedicated but penniless painter?

definitions.meaning: the belief that art needs no moral or practical purpose
an artist working without pay paints purely out of devotion to the work itself

explanation.surface: A belief held by a poor but devoted artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan of the aesthetic movement says beauty needs no purpose, and an unpaid painter works purely out of devotion.

clue.text: Bitter regret suffered by sappers receiving a coded signal

indicators.note: the second piece is received after the first, joined on behind

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are army engineers known as sappers
Morse code is a system of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Soldiers feel sorry after getting a secret message.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are the Royal Engineers, the British army's corps of engineers; 'suffered by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep sorrow for a wrong done.

clue.text: Incidentally, a supporter gets so upset

parts.note: a prop holds something up

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: By the way, a fan becomes distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used as an aside, means by the way.

clue.text: The French politician is a leading light

parts.note: la is French for the
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A French politician is a prominent figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading light' looks like a star figure but means a source of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp gives off light, guiding the way.

clue.text: Go off for a holiday

definitions.meaning: to depart
time away from work, as on military or annual ...

explanation.surface: Head away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go, and permitted time away from work is a break.

clue.text: A prison in a state of agitation

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail in uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means stirred up, in motion and excitement.

clue.text: At liberty now that no charge is being made

definitions.meaning: not imprisoned
costing nothing, without payment

explanation.surface: Released now that the case has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an accusation, but it is a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone released is unconfined, and something given away costs nothing.

clue.text: Just a swings and roundabouts situation

definitions.meaning: even-handed
a funfair, full of rides such as swings and roundabouts

explanation.surface: A thought that a give-and-take outcome is even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swings and roundabouts' is a British idiom for gains balancing losses, but here it names funfair rides; a roundabout is a merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means equitable, and a funfair has rides like swings and merry-go-rounds.

clue.text: He hopes to make a quick buck!

definitions.text: He hopes to make a quick buck!

parts.words: He hopes to make a quick buck!
parts.note: a share speculator buys new issues to sell at once for profit, and a male deer is a buck

explanation.surface: A speculator out for fast money.
explanation.walkthrough: On the stock market a stag buys new shares to sell quickly at a profit; a buck is also a male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A speculator flipping new share issues is called by the name of the male deer.

clue.text: What the plane passenger must pay for dry food

definitions.text: What the plane passenger must pay

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it
fare is food, as on a menu

explanation.surface: A passenger pays for the in-flight meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry food' looks like an in-flight snack but gives AIR plus FARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticket price for a flight.

clue.text: Start taking marijuana and tread the road to ruin

definitions.meaning: read literally as beginning to use cannabis, slang pot
deteriorate, fall into decay

explanation.surface: Taking up cannabis leads to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is turning to cannabis, and idiomatically it means to decay.

clue.text: Strongly denounce vote in the EEC with relative speed

indicators.note: the word in places the voting mark inside the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written: the European Economic Community
X is the mark made on a ballot paper
a rate is speed measured relative to time

explanation.surface: Condemn a ballot in the European Community made in haste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts X inside EEC to give EXEC.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or condemn fiercely.

clue.text: Blustering fellow takes in man of outstanding virtue

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a guy is a fellow
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A loud man houses a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blustering' looks like describing a boastful man but means windy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather blows in blasts, like blustering wind.
